title: Score nord-américain de chylomicronémie familiale (NAFCS)
formula:
The NAFCS is calculated by the addition of the following points:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current age, years | <1* | - |
| ≥1-9 | 12 | |
| ≥10 | - | |
| HTG onset, years (only asked of patients ≥10) | ≥10 | 0 |
| <10 | 12 | |
| [BMI](nabda:calc.body-mass-index-bmi-body-surface-area-bsa\) | ≥25 kg/m² or ≥85 th percentile | 0 |
| <25 kg/m² or <85th percentile | 9 | |
| History of pancreatitis | Neither abdominal pain nor pancreatitis | 0 |
| Abdominal pain but no pancreatitis | 9 | |
| Pancreatitis | 16 | |
| Presence of secondary factors** that may contribute to HTG | ≥1 | 0 |
| None | 11 | |
| Laboratory Values | | |
| All TG >880 mg/dL | No | 0 |
| Yes | 13 | |
| Ratio TG/ TC >8 (when measured in mg/dL) | No | 0 |
| Yes | 8 | |
| Apo B <1.0 g/L | No | 0 |
| Yes | 12 | |

*Calculator cannot be used for patients <1 year old. If infant presents with no secondary factors that may contribute to HTG, consider a diagnosis of FCS. If infant presents with ≥1 secondary factor that may contribute to HTG, but with 2 TG readings >880 mg/dL and unexplained failure to thrive, consider a diagnosis of FCS.

**See list of secondary factors[here](https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/cdn-web-img.mdcalc.com/nafcs_secondary_factors.pdf).

Additional points added:

1. If patient is ≥1-9 years old AND has no secondary factors, +7.
2. If ratio TG/TC >8 AND apo B <1.0 g/dL, +7.
3. If ratio TG/TC >8 AND has no secondary factors, +5.

how_to_use.why:
- FCS is rare and difficult to diagnose, with overlapping features with MCS.
- High scores are highly specific for FCS, potentially allowing a fast-track for genetic testing, specialist referral, and appropriate therapy while avoiding unnecessary work-up with low scores.
- Unlike the Moulin score, this tool incorporates TG/TC ratio, apo B, and BMI.
- Easier to implement than some proposed diagnostic algorithms and requires no specialized laboratory assays.
how_to_use.when:
- Apply in non-pregnant patients ≥1 year old with fasting triglycerides (TG) ≥440 mg/dL to distinguish familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) from multifactorial chylomicronemia (MCS).
- In patients >10 years old, use only in those whose triglycerides are non-responsive to fibrate +/- high-dose omega-3 therapy (i.e. TG decrease <20% from treatment).
how_to_use.pearls:
- Validation is limited to one lipid-clinic cohort of 75 patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia (Western University, Ontario).
- Study excluded:

 - Pregnant individuals.
 - Infants <1 year of age.
 - Patients whose TGs fell ≥20% on fibrate and omega-3 therapy.
 - Those with genetically-confirmed partial lipodystrophy.
 - Anyone with TG level <440 mg/dL.
- A threshold ≥60 is 100% specific but only 67% sensitive for classical FCS; a cutoff of ≥45 still missed about 11% of genetically-proven FCS; thus, it is great for ruling in but poor for excluding the diagnosis.
- Less effective at distinguishing functional FCS from MCS.
- Those with adolescent- or adult-onset hypertriglyceridemia may end up with lower scores and a lower probability of being properly identified; genetic testing may still be warranted in those with scores of 30–44.
- Diagnosis definitions used:

 - Classical FCS: proven biallelic pathogenic variants in one of the canonical genes ( *LPL* , *GPIHBP1* , *APOA5* , *APOC2* , *LMF1* ).
 - MCS: no biallelic variants; may carry a single heterozygous pathogenic variant, have a polygenic TG score > 90th percentile, or have neither.
 - Functional FCS: MCS subset with persistent TG >880 mg/dL.

next_steps.advice:
- Use the results of this tool alongside clinical judgment and, where possible, lipid or genetics-specialist expertise; it should not be the sole determinant of diagnosis or management.
- A high score is highly specific but not diagnostic.
- Results may direct when to perform genetic testing (i.e., scores ≥30-44) and when to initiate FCS-specific therapy while awaiting genetic testing results (i.e., scores ≥60).
